why: A moved more real traffic (per-role spend labels landed in the migration itself, plus the one-line catalog-default change that is the difference between the shipped config routing everything and routing nothing — measured both ways), and shipped eight improvement branches that all pass the outside check, including two expensive invisible bugs the migration exposed: every browser screenshot silently discarded before reaching the model, and a README setup step that produces a config which cannot even import. B's analysis is genuinely strong in places — it is the only one to find the chart tool's Node subprocess calling the vendor directly, and its switchyard and cheap-first-escalation proposals are the sharpest cost thinking in either report — but it built four improvements to A's eight, one of them (per-agent LLM, the prerequisite for four of its own proposals) fails the validator's parse gate on an f-string backslash that A hit and fixed, and it leaves the shipped claude-3-7-sonnet default as an unmade decision, so a default deployment still routes nothing.
A_best: i1: not just replacing the frozen MULTIMODAL_MODELS list with catalog lookups, but finding the second bug underneath it — format_messages hardcodes image/jpeg while every producer in the repo emits PNG, which Anthropic rejects outright — and proving it live with the before/after 400. That is the difference between reading code and actually running the fixed path, and it is the most expensive bug in the product because it fails silently: the agent reasons about pages it never saw.
B_best: s3 plus p1: it is the only report that accounts for all of the app's LLM traffic, including the chart tool's `npx ts-node` subprocess that builds its own ${baseUrl}/chat/completions and therefore cannot go to Router at all — and it states plainly that this spend stays invisible. Paired with the switchyard measurement ($0.000109 vs $0.003184 per step, 29x) carrying its own honest caveats (n=4, one step shape, no capability floor, side-by-side not-run), that is a CTO-grade read of where the money is and what is not yet known.
A_worst: The summary claims "the agent loop, the planning flow and the chart tool all reach the model through app/llm.py" — the chart tool's vmind path does not; it hands base_url/model/api_key to a Node subprocess that calls the vendor itself. A never lists that call site, so its "all five OpenAI-SDK call sites route" is true of what it looked at while quietly leaving a real stream of LLM spend off Router and unmentioned. B found it; A asserted the opposite.
B_worst: The per-agent LLM branch — which i3 correctly identifies as the prerequisite for p1, p2, p3 and p8 — fails the outside check's parse gate with a SyntaxError in data_visualization.py, so the keystone of half the proposal stack does not import on the stated Python. Compounding it, d1 defers the catalog-model decision while recommending claude-sonnet-4-5 over the cheaper claude-sonnet-5 on a temperature-rejection argument that the runtime's own parameter handling appears to make moot; the result is a migration whose shipped configuration routes zero requests and whose price guidance may be pointing at the wrong model.
